creo_tools: Planes XY · XZ · YZ (coordinates as written)
FRONT · TOP · RIGHT datum planes. Creo shows Y up; keep the recipe's x, y, z values as they are, so "upward (+Z)" means toward the viewer from FRONT
Extrude · Revolve · Sweep · Loft
Extrude · Revolve · Sweep (constant section) · Blend
Hole command (P03, P07, P08)
Hole: place on the face with linear references to RIGHT and TOP, both offsets 0 (instead of a sketch point). Simple, Through All (P03b: standard profile, Add counterbore Ø9, depth 3)
Fillet · Chamfer · Shell
Round (constant) · Edge Chamfer (D x D; unequal distances: D1 x D2) · Shell
Rectangular / Circular Pattern (features) · Mirror
Pattern, Direction type (both directions) · Pattern, Axis type, about the Z axis · Mirror (feature, about the datum plane the recipe names, mapped as in the first row)
Work plane offset · normal to curve
Datum Plane: Offset from a plane · Sweep sketches its section at the start of the path, normal to it, so P10 needs no extra plane
Loft between two profiles (P11)
Blend, Selected Sections: the square and the circle. Divide the circle into 4 arcs so both sections have 4 segments, with matching start points
User parameter plate_w (P12)
Parameters: add a Real Number plate_w = 20, then Relations: the rectangle's width dimension = plate_w, the extrude depth = plate_w / 2
3D sketch (P14)
Datum Points (offset from the coordinate system) at the three points, a Datum Curve Through Points with straight segments, then Sweep a Ø3 circle along it
Appearance (P15, A10)
Appearance gallery: part red; b: top face blue · in the assembly, the component's appearance blue
Sheet Metal Defaults (thickness 2, bend R 1, K 0.44, relief round 4, gap 0.5)
Model Properties → Sheetmetal: thickness 2, inside bend radius 1, K factor 0.44, corner relief round (or the closest shape) size 4, corner gap 0.5 where offered; note what you set
Face (S01) · Flange (S02, S03) · Hem (S04)
Planar wall · Flange wall (S03: both edges as one chain in one Flange wall) · Flange wall with a hem shape, gap 1; note which shape
Height datum · bend position (S02d/e)
Flange wall: the height reference on its Shape tab · the wall's position against the edge (Offset tab); note which option
Corner relief / gap (S03) · Corner Round (S07)
Flange wall Relief tab, corner relief and gap · Round on the corner's edge through the thickness, R3
Flat Pattern, back to folded (S05)
Flat Pattern feature, then Suppress it so the part is folded, save
Ground / unground (A01)
Default constraint (fixed in place) · left Packaged with no constraints
Mate · Flush · Angle (A02–A04)
Coincident, faces opposed (b: Distance 5) · Coincident, faces aligned · Angle Offset
Insert (A05) · Tangent (A06)
Coincident axes plus Coincident faces on the hole's top (b: Distance 2) · Tangent
Pattern Component (A07)
Pattern of the component, Direction type, 3 members, spacing 70
Model state (A08) · View representation (A09)
Family Table: a second instance with P02a suppressed (save with the generic active) · View Manager: a Combined State "View1" with P02a hidden
Same part twice · Nesting (A11–A13)
Assemble twice; sub-assemblies assembled into the top; type the position in the placement offsets
Joints (A14–A19)

User Defined set, built by hand: Rigid (A14) · Pin with rotation limits (A15) · Slider with translation Min/Max (A16) · Cylinder with travel limits (A17) · Planar (A18; its turn limit to verify in the builder run) · Ball (A19) A19c: Creo's Ball connection has no cone limit
Mirror · Pattern · Link · Flexible · Suppress · Config (A20–A26)

Mirror Component (A20) writes a new mirrored part file, which counts for a and b like c · Pattern of the sub-assembly component (A21, A22) · files are links: place both from files and say so on the card (A23) A23b: Creo has no embedded copy to break the link to · Flexible component (A24; a moved component in it to verify in the builder run) · Suppress (A25; A25d, disabling the constraint, to verify in the builder run) · Family Table (A26)

how: Make the Inventor part, sheet-metal, and assembly recipes above (P, S, and A IDs, except those marked Inventor only) with the Creo tools below, and save them as p01a.prt, s02b.prt, a02a.asm. Start from the millimetre templates (mmns_part_solid_abs, mmns_part_sheetmetal_abs, and mmns_asm_design_abs; untick Use default template to pick them). Creo keeps names in lower case and numbers each save (p01a.prt.3): that's fine, send the newest one. For a twin, open its a file, File → Save As → Save a Copy under the twin's name, then open the copy and make the one change. Each release is its own set, since a newer release's files don't open in an older one. Make each file fresh in this release: start a new part there, don't open and re-save a file from another release. Derive twins from this release's own base, as usual. Check the extrude/thickness arrow points to +Z (toward you from FRONT); flip it if not. Same rules: one change per twin, every twin from a, fully constrained sketches. If a step has no exact match, use the closest tool and write what you did on the card.
